correctness.rationale: The shell transfer equations follow by the three inverse branches, including the missing halving inverse on I_0. The small formal kernel roots are t(z) and 2t(z); substitution into the numerator equations is legitimate since t(0)=0. Subtracting μ²/(1−z) removes the unit pole, and the remaining factors listed in the record do not vanish for |z|≤1 when p>1/2. Independently one can evaluate the sum without the shell resolvent: let r=q/p, K have invariant law (1−r)r^k, and U be independent uniform; X=2^(−K)U has the stated stationary density by mixing the uniforms on [0,2^(−k)]. Halving increases K; doubling decreases positive K, and at K=0 instead replaces U by 2U mod 1. These updates preserve the product stationary law on (K,U). Put δ(k)=2^(−k), m=Eδ, n=Eδ², b=2/(3p−1). For the reflected depth operator Q, (I−Q)H=δ−m with H(k)=−b(δ(k)+k). For R obtained by discounting the doubling-at-zero transition by 1/2, (I−R)L=δ with L=b(3−δ). Both identities follow by substitution also at k=0. Uniform doubling has lag-j centered covariance 2^(−j)/12, so C_l=Cov(δ(K_0),δ(K_l))/4+E[δ(K_0)(R^lδ)(K_0)]/12. Both terms are nonnegative: monotone coupling preserves depth order, and R is positive. Telescoping sums gives C(1)=E[(δ−m)H]/4+E[δL]/12: reflected chains driven by common choices coalesce when the larger depth first hits zero, with pre-coalescence distance bounded by initial distance, and the number of discounted doublings goes to infinity by the positive doubling-minus-halving drift. Thus the two remainder terms vanish by domination. Using m=2(2p−1)/(3p−1), n=4(2p−1)/(5p−1) and Cov(δ,K)=−2pq/(3p−1)² gives the recorded C(1) and the stated Γ=2C(1)−(n/3−m²/4). Numerical cross-check of this independent evaluation and the rational formula at six parameters including p=1, p=3/5 and p=0.500001 agreed within 7×10⁻¹⁵; the identities, not the grid, establish the theorem. The derivative cubic is positive at 1/2 and increasing, while Var(X_0)∼(8/9)(2p−1); at fixed N the variance per step is at most N Var(X_0), verifying both orders of limits with the separate critical atom.
